There we were. Faced with a modern day Mexican Standoff, I had my gun trained on the man in the black mask. He, in turn had his pistol pointed at Calabrese. And of course, as these things go, Calabrese was pointing his gun at me. So you may be asking yourself, how I managed to get myself into this mess.

Well it’s a long story, but to get to the point, the junkie in the mask stole my dog and is trying to extort me for 5 grand, while Little Tony Calabrese says it’s time to pay up on that gambling debt I owe. Calabrese doesn’t really want to kill anyone and if he kills the man in the mask before I do, he knows I’ll lose my dog and he’ll never see his fucking money. That’s why he’s pointing the gun at me. He's afraid I’ll kill the Mask if I don’t get my dog back, and he’s right, I will. I'm guessing he followed me here and thought this warehouse was as good a place as any to collect.

This idiot in the mask thinks he’s in control because he called me here, but that’s not how these things work. You see, the one in control is always the one with the most to lose. He’s got his gun on Little Cali because he thinks Little Cali’s gonna shoot me and then he won't get his 5. What the both of them don't understand is that no one, except me, is shooting anyone.

So, that's that. You get the idea.

 

I lowered my gun to my side while the other two jack-offs just stood there, suddenly caught off guard. Calabrese, confused now, quickly redirected his aim to the man in the mask. As Little Cali moved to shift his aim, I fired one shot from the hip, hitting him in the ribs. He dropped to the floor and began writhing in pain, coughing up blood as he gasped for air.

As soon as I pulled the trigger I took two giant strides toward the Mask and stuck the crown of my muzzle on the tip of his nose. He stood there in disbelief with his gun still pointing at Calabrese. I reached out with my other hand and pulled his gun away from him.

“Where’s my dog, asshole,” I said as he stared cross-eyed down at my gun. He began to stutter as he tried to tell me my dog was somewhere safe.

“That’s not what I asked,” I replied. I pointed the gun to the floor and fired a shot into his foot. He screamed in pain and fell to the ground. Leaning over him, I asked him again.

“He’s in the van! The van out back! Please, please don’t hurt me!” He screamed as his pants were now soaked in urine and the blood dripped on the floor from his foot. I expressed my appreciation for his swift cooperation and in so many words, reminded him to always do the right thing.

“If you ever fuck with me or my dog again, I’ll fucking kill you,” I said as I jabbed a finger in his chest. The man in the mask nodded his head, got up and hobbled out the side door. I turned to walk away but stopped to look at Calabrese. Not much hope for him since the sporadic guppy breathing had started and the blood continued to pool out of his mouth. His people will be looking for him when he misses the family dinner. That’s the thing about the Calabrese family dinners, you only miss out if you’re locked up or dead. Little Cali wasn’t quite dead yet, but he was getting there. What the fuck am I doing here thinking about this shit, I thought to myself, I gotta get out of here.

I left out the back door and could hear Max whining in the van. I opened the back hatch of the van and quickly untied him. He immediately jumped into my arms unable to hold back his crying while he licked my face in excitement. I gotta quit making friends with the wrong people, I thought to myself as I took his leash and we headed home. I knew we’d be on the run again soon, but I was okay with that as long as Max was with me.
